name: bld5_isometries_compact_simultaneous_recurrence
statement: {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y) (hf : Isometry f) (hg : Isometry g) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) x < ε) ∧ ∀ y : Y, dist (g^[n] y) y < ε
closed: ∀ {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type*} [MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y) (hf : Isometry f) (hg : Isometry g) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε), ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (∀ x : X, dist (f^[n] x) x < ε) ∧ ∀ y : Y, dist (g^[n] y) y < ε
informal: Uses Mathlib2.bld4_isometry_compact_uniform_recurrence: apply it to Prod.map f g on the compact metric space X × Y (sup metric; Prod.map of isometries is an isometry, and (Prod.map f g)^[n] = Prod.map f^[n] g^[n]) to get n > 0 with dist((f^[n] x, g^[n] y), (x, y)) < ε for all (x, y); Prod.dist_eq (max) splits it into the two components. If X or Y is empty apply the theorem to the other factor alone.
type: ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : MetricSpace X] [CompactSpace X] {Y : Type u_2} [inst_2 : MetricSpace Y] [CompactSpace Y] (f : X → X) (g : Y → Y), Isometry f → Isometry g → ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ n, 0 < n ∧ (∀ (x : X), dist (f^[n] x) x < ε) ∧ ∀ (y : Y), dist (g^[n] y) y < ε
